judged_text: The conditional refactor inverts the billing flag for slug assignment: the old code wrote slug only when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED was false (!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }), the new code writes it only when true (IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}), while the requestedSlug line's meaning is unchanged. On billing-disabled (self-hosted) deployments organizations are created with neither slug nor requestedSlug, silently dropping the org's URL handle entirely; on billing-enabled deployments the slug is now claimed in the database at creation time before payment, where it was previously deferred to a requestedSlug pending billing.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts`, the condition for writing `slug` to `organization.create` was flipped from `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. Meanwhile `metadata.requestedSlug` remains gated by `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED`. From the diff alone, when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is false, neither `slug` nor `metadata.requestedSlug` will be written, whereas previously `slug` would be written. When `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is true, `slug` is now written immediately (previously only `requestedSlug` was). This matches the finding’s described inversion and implies a real behavior regression/data omission.
